notes: IDENTITY REFUTED (research 2026-07-03): 'Mary Blackmore, wife of Thomas Larkin and mother of Ellen' does not exist. FreeBMD (coverage essentially complete for the period): NO Larkin x Blackmore marriage anywhere in England & Wales 1885-1911. The five baptisms on this record (Lynton 1852, Broadclyst 1864, Wigan 1867, 1871, 1886) are five different Mary Blackmores; the 1871/1881/1891 censuses belong to yet others.

The '25 Dec 1905 St Lukes Ramsgate' marriage belongs to Mary Ellen BLACKMORE of Elham district (Folkestone, not Ramsgate), who married Hubert Elliott or William Henry Sneddon (GRO Dec Q 1905, 2a/2421). No Thomas Larkin married in Thanet that quarter. The St Lawrence Ramsgate register for 25 Dec 1905 shows Hill x Monk.

The one genuinely relevant record hiding in this chimera is the death: MARY ELLEN LARKIN, aged 42 (b. ~1863/64), Mar Q 1906, WHITEHAVEN 10b/429 (not Lancashire, and a Larkin record, not Blackmore). She may have been Thomas Larkin's wife — but a woman who died Mar 1906 cannot be the mother of Ellen (b. ~Nov 1906). Her death certificate would show her husband.

Ellen's actual mother: UNKNOWN pending one lookup — GRO online index (free account at gro.gov.uk), Births Mar Q 1907, Whitehaven 10b/689, LARKIN Ellen: the mother's-maiden-name column answers this. Same lookup for probable brother Samuel Larkin (Jun Q 1903, Whitehaven 10b/733).
CASE CLOSED (2026-07-03): the tree owner's GRO lookup on Ellen's registration returned maiden name McALONE — confirming this Blackmore identity has no place in the line.

PARENTAGE REINSTATED (2026-07-03, PR #7 review comment): the tree owner stated 'Thomas Larkin and Mary Blackmore are correct' as Ellen M Larkin's (I182195857362) parents, overriding the McAlone/William Larkin (M0001/M0003) finding above. Ellen's relationships.parents has been restored to point at this record. The GRO-based contradictions noted above (no Larkin x Blackmore marriage in the GRO index, the 1911 census household headed by William Larkin) have not been independently re-resolved — flagging for future reconciliation.
